official.deadline_note: No single calendar deadline is published. The annual cycle runs: graduate school admission (~Nov) - recommendation submission by the graduate school (~Dec) - interview by the Foundation (~Jan) - final selection announcement (~Feb) - certificate award ceremony (Mar).
official.application_cycle: Annual intake with a March certificate award ceremony; entry begins with graduate school admission around November
official.status_note: The Foundation presents this as a standing annual programme (20 students per year, subject to change); 2026 fellows are already listed and the next cycle follows the same November-to-March timetable.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Master's program: Full tuition for 4 semesters. Doctoral program / Integrated Master's and Doctoral program: Full tuition for 6 semesters.
benefits: Master's program: Full tuition for 4 semesters and living expenses for 22 months (KRW 1,000,000/month)
Doctoral program / Integrated Master's and Doctoral program: Full tuition for 6 semesters and living expenses for 36 months (KRW 1,000,000/month)
Initial settlement fee of KRW 1,000,000 (one-time payment), National Health Insurance premium (NHIS), etc.
Support for Korean language education, certificate award ceremonies, welfare services, Korean cultural experience programs, etc.
eligibility: Applicants must hold (or be expected to hold) a Bachelor's degree and possess a non-Korean nationality; applicants with Korean citizenship, including dual citizenship holders, are not eligible
Applicants must have been admitted to a Master's or Doctoral program at a Korean graduate school and must be recommended by their admitting institution

Eligible countries (tentative): Asia - China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, Vietnam; Americas - Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, United States; Europe - Germany, Italy, Poland, Slovakia, Turkiye, United Kingdom; Africa - Egypt, Morocco, South Africa
Eligible universities (tentative): KDI School of Public Policy and Management, Korea University, POSTECH, Seoul National University, The Academy of Korean Studies, Yonsei University
Applicants may apply for majors in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences/engineering
requirements: Admission to a Master's or Doctoral program at an eligible Korean graduate school (the entry route)
Recommendation by the admitting graduate school, submitted to the Foundation around December
Interview by the Foundation for candidates moving to final selection (around January)
coverage: Tuition (full, for 4 semesters Master's / 6 semesters doctoral)
Living expenses: KRW 1,000,000 per month for 22 months (Master's) or 36 months (doctoral)
Korean language education and Korean cultural experience programmes
application_method: Graduate school admission at an eligible Korean university (~Nov)
Recommendation submission by the graduate school to the Foundation (~Dec)
official.application_route: No direct application to the Foundation: gain admission to a Master's or Doctoral program at one of the designated Korean graduate schools, then be recommended by that school.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-Korean nationality required; applicants with Korean citizenship, including dual citizenship holders, are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Open to non-Korean nationals from the listed eligible countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Majors in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences/engineering at six designated graduate schools (lists marked tentative)
official.duration: Master's program: 4 semesters of tuition support and 22 months of living expenses. Doctoral program / Integrated Master's and Doctoral program: 6 semesters of tuition support and 36 months of living expenses.
official.description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea, presented by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation as 'The Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program', is the Foundation's in-bound scholarship that invites non-Korean talent to Korea to complete Master's or Doctoral degrees at designated graduate schools. It offers full tuition and living expenses so awardees build connections with Korean society and become globally minded leaders bridging their home countries and Korea.
official.program_type: Private-sector foundation scholarship administered by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation (POSCO Group)

verification.notes: Amounts, coverage, eligibility, selection timetable and country/university lists taken from the Foundation's own programme, FAQ and purpose pages; the Foundation marks both the country and university lists as tentative. Selection is capped at 20 students per year (subject to change).

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a two-stage race: the scholarship only opens after you are admitted to one of six designated Korean graduate schools and nominated by that school around December, so the real deadline is your graduate admission, not anything the Foundation publishes. Funding is full tuition for four semesters (Master's) or six (doctoral) plus KRW 1,000,000 a month for 22 or 36 months, a one-off KRW 1,000,000 settlement fee and NHIS coverage.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-Korean applicants from the listed countries aiming for a Master's or PhD at SNU, Yonsei, Korea University, POSTECH, KDI School or the Academy of Korean Studies.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure graduate admission first at a designated university - nomination is impossible without an offer
Verify your nationality is on the Foundation's tentative eligible-country list and that you hold no Korean citizenship
In November, ask your admitting school's graduate or international office who files the Foundation recommendation and what they need from you
Prepare for the Foundation interview held around January
Re-check the Foundation notice board each autumn, because both the country and university lists are marked tentative and can change
common_rejection_risks: Holding Korean citizenship, including as a dual national - an absolute bar
Being admitted to a university outside the six designated schools
Choosing a major outside the humanities, social sciences or natural sciences/engineering
Waiting for a Foundation application window that never comes and missing the school's December nomination
Enrolling on a programme whose remaining semesters fall outside the 22/36-month support period, leaving the final stretch unfunded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package covers tuition, the monthly allowance, the settlement fee and NHIS premiums; airfare, visa and residence fees, and living costs above KRW 1,000,000 a month are not published as covered and should be self-funded.
document_audit: The Foundation publishes no document checklist, so the nominating graduate school defines the de facto package - request it from the international office early
Expect to evidence non-Korean nationality, since dual citizenship is an absolute disqualifier
Because the Foundation interviews candidates directly in January, be ready to speak fluently about your study plan even though no written list is published
alerts: Only about 20 scholars are selected per year worldwide (subject to change)
Both the eligible-country and eligible-university lists are explicitly marked tentative and can shift between cycles
Selection is multi-stage: school recommendation in December, Foundation interview in January, announcement in February
The cycle culminates in a March certificate award ceremony, so plan your arrival around the spring semester
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Graduate admission at a designated school in autumn -> school recommendation to the Foundation in December -> Foundation interview in January -> final announcement in February -> award ceremony in March.

official.deadline_note: NIIED publishes no central deadline on the programme page; application timing is set by each Korean university selected to operate the programme, so deadlines vary by affiliated university.
official.status_note: Standing annual programme described on NIIED's live programme page; support runs for one 4-month semester and selection is routed through universities NIIED has chosen to operate the programme.
benefits: Round-trip airfare: economy class airfare based on the actual cost
The grants cover the expenses for accommodation, settlement, airfare, and insurance fee
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate (Master's and Doctoral degree) students of foreign nationality who are enrolled in an overseas university that have agreements with a Korean university affiliated with NIIED
Applicants whose overall academic performance at their home university is 80% or above
Applicants must be enrolled in a degree exchange program (those enrolled solely in Korean language courses are excluded)
Applicants who have previously received scholarship from the Korean government are not eligible
Dual nationals who hold Korean citizenship are not eligible
requirements: Enrollment in a degree exchange program (applicants enrolled solely in Korean language courses are excluded)
Overall academic performance at the home university of 80% or above
Recommendation by a Korean university selected by NIIED to operate the programme
application_method: NIIED selects universities to operate the GKS Exchange Students Program
The selected university recommends scholarship applicants
NIIED reviews and selects the recommended applicants
official.application_route: Apply through a Korean university that NIIED has selected to operate the programme; individual applications to NIIED are not accepted.
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign nationality required; dual nationals who hold Korean citizenship are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Open to foreign nationals enrolled at overseas universities holding agreements with NIIED-affiliated Korean universities
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Degree exchange program only; applicants enrolled solely in Korean language courses are excluded
official.description: The GKS Non-degree Program for Foreign Exchange Students offers financial support for selected international exchange students at affiliated universities in Korea, with grants covering accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance fees plus a monthly allowance for a single 4-month semester.
official.program_type: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) Program, operated by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED) under the Ministry of Education

verification.notes: Allowance (KRW 630,000/month), airfare rule, coverage list, 4-month duration, eligibility rules and the two-stage selection procedure taken from NIIED's official programme page; NIIED publishes no central deadline or document list, and the English news board shows no current-cycle notice for this programme.

applicant_utility.summary: Never apply to NIIED directly: your route is your home university's exchange office nominating you to a Korean host university that NIIED has selected to run the programme, with NIIED making the final call. Support is KRW 630,000 per month for a single 4-month semester plus economy round-trip airfare at actual cost, with accommodation, settlement and insurance covered but no tuition.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Current undergraduate or graduate students at partner universities abroad with strong transcripts (80%+) heading to Korea for one credit-bearing exchange semester.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your home university has an agreement with a Korean university operating the GKS programme this cycle
Check that your overall academic performance clears the 80% threshold before your school will nominate you
Make sure your exchange is degree/credit-bearing - Korean-language-only enrollment is excluded
Ask the host Korean university's international office for their nomination deadline and package, since NIIED sets no central date
common_rejection_risks: Enrolling solely in Korean language courses, which the programme explicitly excludes
Having previously received any Korean government scholarship - an absolute bar
Overall performance below 80% at the home university
Sending an individual application to NIIED instead of going through the university route
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition is not among the published grant items; the KRW 630,000 monthly allowance plus actual-cost airfare, accommodation, settlement and insurance cover the stay, so meals, local transport, visa costs and personal spending come from your own funds.
document_audit: NIIED publishes no document list, so the nominating university's exchange office defines what you must submit
Proof of enrollment at your home university and full transcripts evidencing the 80%+ performance will be central to the nomination
Airfare is reimbursed at actual cost, so keep tickets, boarding passes and receipts if you front the money
alerts: Deadlines vary by affiliated university - there is no single national date
Funding covers one 4-month semester only; no Korean degree is awarded and you return to your home institution afterward
NIIED chooses which universities may operate the programme each cycle, so availability shifts year to year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Home university exchange office -> Korean host university (selected by NIIED) nominates you -> NIIED reviews and makes the final selection.
